sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.
2. Records have been placed before this Court to consider the prayer of the sole appellant for suspension of his sentence and release on bail during the pendency of the appeal.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1214 of 2024(10) dt.03-11-2025 3.
The notice has been served upon respondent No. 2 through his wife.
No one has appeared on behalf of the informant to oppose the prayer for suspension of sentence of the appellant.
We have noticed from the deposition of respondent No. 2 that she has been married to someone else and is living in her family with her child.

sentences.text: The appellant has been convicted vide judgment dated 23.07.2024 and sentenced vide order dated 01.08.2024 in connection with G.R. No. 4507 of 2019, arising out Korha P.S. Case No. 395 of 2019, passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-VII-Cum-Special Judge, POCSO Act, Katihar for the offences under Sections 376 and 363 of the Indian Penal Code (in short the 'IPC') and Section 4(1) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (in short the 'POCSO Act').

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-VII-Cum-Special Judge, POCSO Act, Katihar
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
He has been ordered to undergo rigorous imprisonment for fifteen years with a fine of Rs. 50,000/- under Section 4(1) of the POCSO Act and in default of payment of fine, he shall further undergo simple imprisonment for six months and rigorous imprisonment for seven years with a fine of Rs. 25,000/-
for the offence under Section 363 of the IPC and in default of payment of fine, he shall further undergo simple imprisonment for three months.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1214 of 2024(10) dt.03-11-2025 5.
The prosecution case is based on a written information furnished by the father of the victim girl (informant).
He has alleged in the written information that on 03.10.2019, when he had gone to work and his wife had also gone in the field, at about 03:00 P.M. when she returned home, her daughter was not found.
He alleged that his younger daughter told her mother that about 12:00 - 01:00 P.M., one Poonam Devi, wife of Akhilesh Mahaldar had come and taken away the sister, who had yet not returned.
The informant claimed that his wife searched her daughter but when no information was received, then she informed him.
Thereafter, information was given to the police.

He has stated that about 8 - 10 days ago, the named accused persons had threatened his daughter,
aged about 15 years, to kill her, which he had informed to his neighbours.
He expressed his apprehension that the named accused persons had taken away his daughter.
On the basis of the written information, submitted on 04.10.2019 at 18:30 hours, the FIR was registered.

6. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that in this case despite the fact that the informant had come to know about the missing of his daughter on the same day at about 03:00 P.M., the information to this effect was given to the police Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1214 of 2024(10) dt.03-11-2025 after more than twenty four hours, even as the police station is situated at a distance of only three kilometers.
Learned counsel further submits that later on, the victim was recovered and the appellant was arrested from Mahinathpur Chowk on 22.11.2019.

The I.O. (P.W. 9)
has stated that he had recovered the victim girl when she was along with the appellant and had inquired from both of them, whereafter they were brought to the police station.

It has further been submitted that the victim girl has alleged that on 03.10.2019 at 09:00 A.M. in the morning, when she was cooking foods, at that time, one Poonam Devi came and she had taken her away to her home, where, after taking breakfast, she had become unconscious and when she regained her consciousness, then Poonam Devi told her that she was in Bhagalpur.
She named some persons including the appellant, who were present there.
She has then alleged that at the instance of Poonam Devi, she was made to stay with the appellant, who had committed rape with her for three days and he kept her with himself for one and half month.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the medical examination of the victim girl, the Doctor (P.W. 4) has not found any injury on the body or private part.
It is submitted that the age of the victim has been assessed between Patna High Court CR.

2 dt.03-11-2025 15 - 17 years and the defence has suggested that she had gone away with the appellant.

sentences.text:
It has lastly been submitted that as against the maximum sentence of fifteen years, the appellant has already spent almost six years in incarceration, this appeal is of the year 2024 and is not likely to be heard in near future, therefore this Court may grant privilege of suspension of sentence and bail to the appellant at this stage.
8.
The prayer has been opposed by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

9. Having regard to the submissions noted hereinabove and the kind of the case of the defence coupled with the fact that the appellant has remained in jail for almost six years out of fifteen years awarded to him, but this appeal is not likely to be heard in near future, we direct for suspension of the sentence of the appellant and his release on bail during pendency of the appeal.

10. Let the sentence of the appellant be suspended and he be released on bail, during pendency of the appeal, on his furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/-(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VII-Cum- Special Judge, POCSO Act, Katihar, in connection with G.R. Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1214 of 2024(10) dt.03-11-2025 No. 4507 of 2019, arising out Korha P.S. Case No. 395 of 2019.
11.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-VII-Cum- Special Judge, POCSO Act, Katihar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The fine, if any, imposed as a part of sentence shall remain suspended during pendency of the appeal.

12. It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only prima facie and tentative for the purpose of suspension of sentence and bail only, which would not cause prejudice to either parties.

13. List this appeal for hearing on its turn.
(Rajeev Ranjan Prasad, J) (Sourendra Pandey, J) Praveen-II/-
